title: Reducing belief in conspiracy theories as they unfold using large language models
abstract: arXiv:2608.06151v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The emergence of conspiracy theories in the wake of major events is a significant societal challenge. Here we test whether conversational dialogues with a large language model (LLM) can reduce belief in immediately unfolding conspiracies. In experiments conducted in the days following the July 2024 assassination attempt on Donald Trump and the September 2025 assassination of Charlie Kirk, U.S. adults (Experiment 1: N = 472; Experiment 2: N = 1042) holding conspiratorial views about the crisis event engaged in a multi-turn conversation with an LLM prompted to reduce their conspiracy belief. Compared to control participants who either discussed an irrelevant topic with an LLM or viewed a static fact sheet, participants in the LLM treatment showed significantly reduced conspiracy beliefs in both experiments. translated_title: 利用在阴谋论演变过程中与之对话的大语言模型降低阴谋论信念
translated_abstract: 重大事件发生后阴谋论的出现是一个重要的社会挑战。本研究测试了与大语言模型（LLM）进行对话能否减少人们对正在发酵中的阴谋的信念。在2024年7月唐纳德·特朗普遇刺未遂事件和2025年9月查理·柯克遇刺事件发生后的数天内进行的实验中，持有关于该危机事件阴谋论观点的美国成年人（实验1：N = 472；实验2：N = 1042）与一个被设定为降低其阴谋论信念的大语言模型进行了多轮对话。与控制组参与者（他们要么与大语言模型讨论无关话题，要么阅读静态的事实清单）相比，接受大语言模型干预的参与者在两项实验中都表现出显著降低的阴谋论信念。我们还发现了一些关于大语言模型干预产生下游效应的提示性证据，观察到对部分（但非全部）——
tldr: 在真实重大危机事件发生后的数天内，与大语言模型进行多轮对话能够显著降低美国成年人对正在兴起的阴谋论的信念，并可能产生一定的下游影响。
en_tdlr: Multi-turn conversations with a large language model can significantly reduce belief in conspiracy theories as they unfold in the days immediately following major real-world crisis events.
